healthy.disease_description: The photo did not show signs of the three lettuce diseases GreenGuard checks for.
healthy.pathogen_description: There is no associated pathogen for this result. A photo may miss early symptoms or problems outside the scanned area.
treatment_recommendations: No disease treatment is indicated by this photo.
Keep checking new leaves and the underside of leaves. Maintain good spacing and clean tools.
healthy.selling_explanation: The photo showed no signs of the supported diseases. Inspect the whole head and use normal harvesting and handling checks before selling.

downy mildew.disease_description: Look for yellow patches on top of leaves and pale, fuzzy growth underneath.
downy mildew.pathogen_description: Bremia lactucae is a fungus-like organism associated with lettuce downy mildew. The photo suggests the disease but cannot confirm the organism.
treatment_recommendations: Remove badly affected leaves or plants and clear diseased debris from the bed.
Space plants so air can move. Water near the roots to help leaves stay dry.
Look under nearby leaves and ask a local agriculture technician about treatments approved for lettuce if symptoms spread.
downy mildew.selling_explanation: Separate affected heads from healthy produce. Yellow or fuzzy leaves reduce quality, so do not sell visibly affected leaves.

powdery mildew.disease_description: Look for a white or gray powder on the leaf surface. Older leaves may turn yellow.
powdery mildew.pathogen_description: This fungus grows on lettuce leaves and forms the powdery coating. A photo cannot confirm the species.
treatment_recommendations: Remove badly affected leaves and clear diseased crop debris.
Give plants room for airflow and check both sides of nearby leaves.
Ask a local agriculture technician about locally approved lettuce treatments if the coating spreads.
powdery mildew.selling_explanation: The powdery coating can affect appearance and quality. Keep affected heads separate and do not sell visibly coated or damaged leaves.

septoria blight.disease_description: This leaf spot disease can cause brown spots that grow larger and damage the leaf.
septoria blight.pathogen_description: Septoria lactucae is a fungus associated with lettuce Septoria leaf spot. Other problems can produce similar spots, so inspect the plant in person.
treatment_recommendations: Remove spotted leaves and clear diseased crop debris from the bed.
Water near the roots to reduce splashing. Avoid handling plants while the leaves are wet.
Check nearby heads and seek local crop advice if spotting continues.
septoria blight.selling_explanation: Spotted or damaged lettuce may not meet market quality. Keep affected heads separate and do not sell visibly damaged leaves.
